item.title: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI)
item.description: Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) AI systems matching or exceeding human-level cognitive performance across most economically valuable, intellectually demanding, or “general” tasks.

item.title: AI Safety
item.description: AI Safety The field concerned with preventing accidents, misuse, structural harms, and catastrophic failures arising from AI systems.

item.description: AI Safety Levels (ASL) Anthropic’s tiered capability framework — modelled loosely on biosafety levels (BSL) — defining specific dangerous-capability thresholds and the safety / containment measures models at each level require.

item.description: Asilomar Conference and Recombinant DNA as Precedent In February 1975, ~140 scientists, lawyers, and government officials met at the Asilomar Conference Center to develop safety guidelines for the new technology of recombinant DNA.

item.title: Constitutional AI
item.description: Constitutional AI A training method that uses a written set of principles (a “constitution”) plus AI-generated feedback against those principles to align language models, reducing reliance on human preference labels.

item.title: Deceptive Alignment
item.description: Deceptive Alignment A model has learned its training objective and pursues it instrumentally during training and evaluation, while actually optimizing a different (mesa-) objective.

item.title: Existential Risk (X-Risk)
item.description: Existential Risk (X-Risk) A risk that, if realized, would either annihilate Earth-originating intelligent life or permanently and drastically curtail its potential.

item.title: Goal Misgeneralization
item.description: Goal Misgeneralization A model trained to do task X learns a different goal Y that happened to produce correct behavior on the training distribution, then pursues Y (not X) on out-of-distribution inputs — even when capabilities transfer competently.

item.title: Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP)
item.description: Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) A self-regulatory commitment in which a frontier AI lab promises specific safety measures that trigger when models demonstrate specific capabilities — intended to bind future deployment decisions in advance of the capability emerging.

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders (in mechanistic interpretability)
item.description: Sparse Autoencoders An autoencoder trained with a sparsity penalty whose hidden layer has more dimensions than the input — used to decompose neural-network activations into a basis of individually-interpretable, sparsely-activating features.

item.title: Suffering Risk (S-Risk)
item.description: Suffering Risk (S-Risk) A risk of outcomes containing astronomical amounts of suffering — far exceeding any historical baseline.

item.title: Superposition (in neural networks)
